name: Smartsheet
subcategory: team projects, issues and delivery planning
tagline: Manage structured project rows with formulas, forms, automations, and reports

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 1–10 paid members, unlimited Contributors, 20 GB storage, 30 MB/attachment and 250 automations/month

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Minimum 3 paid members, unlimited Guests/Contributors, 1 TB storage, 250 MB/attachment and unlimited automations

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Minimum 10 paid members, unlimited storage, enterprise security/admin and premium support options

tiers.name: Advanced Work Management
tiers.limits: Enterprise bundle with Control Center, Dynamic View, Data Shuttle and other advanced capabilities

pricing.hiddenCosts: Business has a 3-member minimum and Enterprise a 10-member minimum. Dynamic View starts at $125/month and Data Shuttle at $100/month; Brandfolder, Resource Management, Control Center and Calendar App are separately quoted. Smartsheet's user-subscription model can turn active collaborators into paid members.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Smartsheet, manage structured project rows with formulas, forms, automations, and reports. The hard boundary is spreadsheet familiarity, enterprise controls, connectors, automation, and scale, plus collaboration, integrations, and organizational trust.
coreLoopDIY: Manage structured project rows with formulas, forms, automations, and reports, and track work through milestones, comments, and a searchable activity history for a small team.
whatYouLose: spreadsheet familiarity, enterprise controls, connectors, automation, and scale
ongoingBurden: auth, permissions, notifications, search, migrations, audit history, integrations, backups, and uptime
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Smartsheet because teams pay because project state has to remain authoritative through staff changes, outages, and years of accumulated workflow exceptions. The recurring cost buys auth, permissions, notifications, search, migrations, audit history, integrations, backups, and uptime, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Plane
priorArt.desc: Active open-source project and issue tracking platform.

alternatives.name: Grist
alternatives.desc: A spreadsheet that grew relations, forms, and dashboards without becoming Smartsheet

facts.install: Hosted signup, desktop app, or Docker container for self-hosting
facts.dataFormat: Each document is a .grist SQLite database containing table data, attachments, document metadata, and recent history; CSV/Excel exports are also available
facts.gapVsPaid: It lacks Smartsheet's mature project dependencies, resource management, cross-sheet reports, and workflow automation built around schedules.
facts.setupBlocker: None for hosted or desktop use; shared self-hosting requires Docker, authentication, backups, a public URL, and safe Python-formula sandboxing

alternatives.name: Baserow
alternatives.desc: Airtable's database half with public forms and your own disk underneath

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker/Docker Compose for self-hosting
facts.dataFormat: Cloud workspaces live in Baserow Cloud; self-hosted records live in PostgreSQL and uploaded files in the mounted Baserow data volume; CSV export is available
facts.gapVsPaid: Baserow can hold project rows but does not match Smartsheet's Gantt dependencies, critical-path planning, portfolio reporting, and resource management.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires Docker, persistent volumes, secrets, and public-URL/TLS configuration

alternatives.name: Teable
alternatives.desc: Airtable-shaped tables, forms, kanban, and automation; AI is where the upsell begins

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose/Kubernetes for self-hosting
facts.engines: AI features can use a configured model provider or self-hosted compatible service; standalone community deployment omits AI and App Builder
facts.dataFormat: Cloud records live in Teable Cloud; self-hosted records live in PostgreSQL, with attachments in local, MinIO, S3, or Aliyun object storage; bases export as .tea backups and tables as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: Teable is an Airtable-like database rather than a project execution suite, so dependencies, portfolio reporting, and resource management are substantially weaker.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs Docker, at least 4 GB RAM, PostgreSQL, secrets, storage, and a public URL; the full AI/App Builder stack is materially heavier than the standalone deployment

rejectedAlternatives.name: NocoDB
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Community has tables and views, but timeline, Gantt, conditional forms, and the richer workflow layer are paid

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a small-team tracker DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Smartsheet in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: manage structured project rows with formulas, forms, automations, and reports, and track work through milestones, comments, and a searchable activity history for a small team.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement organizations, projects, members, issues, labels, cycles, and milestones.
Provide list, kanban, and simple timeline views backed by one canonical issue model.
Add comments, mentions, assignments, watchers, and a complete activity log.
Implement project roles for owner, member, and viewer and test every mutation.
Add search, CSV import or export, email notifications, and daily database backups.
Ship Docker Compose, health checks, migrations, seed data, and an admin recovery command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out hundreds of external integrations.
Deliberately leave out enterprise portfolio planning and SSO.
Deliberately leave out native mobile clients and vendor-operated uptime.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
